findings.detail: The rebuilt probe, both stripped wrapper libraries and all 16 auxiliary libraries load with RTLD_NOW on a guest whose kernel/page size and process sysconf both report 16384. Every wrapper run printed 'PASS dlopen' and its DEVICE line reported page_size=16384. No dependency failed to load and no 16 KB alignment load error was observed; every staged library has LOAD segments aligned to 0x4000 and each wrapper has four LOAD segments at 0x4000.
The read-only caller-data control reproduces on 16 KB: baseline readonly SIGSEGV 9/9 (exit 139, before 'PASS image-and-caller-data'); candidate readonly passes 9/9 including all pixel cycles.

candidate rgba/bc1/bc3 pass 27/27 protocol runs and 12/12 USE_IMAGE_VIEW=1 runs at edges 4/5/16 and cycles 1/8/32; baseline rgba/bc1/bc3 pass 27/27 protocol runs. Pixel round-trip and staging lifetime complete with clean exits.

Without forced wrapper emulation the guest's Goldfish GFXStream Vulkan device (host lavapipe) claims textureCompressionBC but returns undecoded BC block bytes for buffer-image copies. This affects the system loader target (no wrapper) equally, so it is not a wrapper or page-size regression; it means BC1/BC3 qualification on this AVD is only meaningful with FORCE_BCN_EMULATION=1, which is what the 4 KB pass also used.

bc_native_path_observation.question: Why do BC1/BC3 modes need FORCE_BCN_EMULATION=1 on this 16 KB emulator?
bc_native_path_observation.observed: Without FORCE_BCN_EMULATION the wrapper logs 'bc1 support:' / 'bc4 support:' but neither 'Forcing BCn emulation' nor 'Faking feature support for textureCompressionBC'; the image is left in its native format and the probe pixel check fails with rgba=0,248,0,0, i.e. the raw first BC block bytes rather than decoded red. With FORCE_BCN_EMULATION=1 the wrapper logs 'Forcing BCn emulation (disable by setting FORCE_BCN_EMULATION=0)' and 'Faking feature support for textureCompressionBC', and the pixel check passes. 'Forcing BCn emulation' is only logged when the underlying device reports textureCompressionBC, so this guest reports BCn support but its native BC buffer-image copy does not decode.
bc_native_path_observation.system_target_control: The same native-path failure occurs against /system/lib64/libvulkan.so with no wrapper loaded (9/9 system bc1/bc3 protocol runs and 3 task_env runs exit 1 on the pixel check while image creation passes), so it is a property of the emulator's Vulkan device, not of either wrapper build.

limitations: llvmpipe software Vulkan inside the Android emulator via the guest Goldfish GFXStream device (host lavapipe, LLVM 21.1.4), not Adreno/KGSL and not a physical GPU.
No game launch: this probe starts no Steam, Wine, window or game; no game frame is rendered.
No performance/FPS measurement; cycles count synchronous probe iterations, not frame time or throughput.

The probe exercises only Vulkan create-image, BC1/BC3 decode through buffer-image copy, the read-only caller format-list path and a copy round-trip; it does not cover drawing, sampling, presentation, staging lifetime under concurrency or image quality.
Inputs are hidden/synthetic probe buffers and pixels generated by tools/tests/vulkan-wrapper-native.c, not game assets.
The candidate and baseline are build-tree libraries; the wrapper is not packaged or installed by Vapor and no app asset, runtime selection or release output changed.
BC1/BC3 results depend on FORCE_BCN_EMULATION=1 because the emulator's native BC buffer-image copy is wrong; no claim about native BC on a physical GPU follows.
The 4 KB AVD was not rerun; its results are referenced, with hash/identity cross-checks, not reproduced.

Only 16 KB page size was exercised in this pass; no matched 4 KB-vs-16 KB differential was produced here, and the 16 KB AVD uses a different Android version (17/API 37) and GPU backend than the 4 KB AVD (Android 16/API 36).
USE_IMAGE_VIEW=1 was only sampled for baseline/candidate bc1/bc3 at cycles 8, edges 4/5/16.
Emulator was cold-booted with -no-snapshot-load/-no-snapshot-save on port 5556 with -gpu lavapipe and -memory 3072; results are tied to that launch.
